{"body":"<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/668
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

## What

Adds the ability to import a coding agent's pre-existing local transcripts into Entire as read-only checkpoints, so a repo adopting Entire isn't starting from zero (`checkpoint list`/`explain`, `search`, `tokens`, and server-side recap/UI work on day-one history). Partially #1336 (enable doesn't prompt to import yet - requires manual kickoff for validation first). Claude Code is the only agent implemented; the package is structured so others can be added.

Surface: a hidden command, discoverable via `entire labs`:

```
entire import claude-code [--path DIR] [--dry-run] [--session ID]...
```

There is intentionally **no** enable-time prompt this pass — importing is an explicit, opt-in command.

## How

- New `cmd/entire/cli/agentimport/` package. The orchestration (discovery loop, idempotent per-turn IDs, redaction, checkpoint write) is agent-agnostic; each agent plugs in an `Importer` (`Discover` + `SplitTurns`). A static list of supported importers backs `entire import <agent>` — adding an agent is a new `Importer`, no command wiring.
- Discovers `~/.claude/projects/<sanitized-repo-path>/*.jsonl` (fixed **one-month** lookback), splits each session into **per-user-prompt turns**, and writes one checkpoint per turn — reusing existing transcript parsing, per-turn token accounting (incl. subagent rollups), and redaction (`redact.JSONLBytes`).
- Imported checkpoints are stored on the normal `entire/checkpoints/v1` metadata branch, tagged `Kind:"imported"` with provenance (source, session/turn UUIDs, line range, content hash, import version). They're **commit-less** (no `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer) and surface in `list`/`explain` via an `Imported` flag, labeled `[imported]`.
- **Idempotent**: per-turn checkpoint IDs are `sha256(sessionID + "/" + turnUUID)`, so re-running skips already-imported turns.
- **Not rewindable**: `checkpoint rewind` refuses imported checkpoints with a clear read-only message.

## Tradeoffs / known limitations (do later)

- **Import is manual.** It is not offered during `entire enable` (an earlier iteration prompted at enable time; removed for now). Users run `entire import claude-code` when they want it.
- **Imported history is pushed** to the backend like normal checkpoints (it's what lights up server-side search/recap/UI). **Privacy note:** up to a month of old conversations (and provenance such as `transcript_path`) sync on the next push, unless checkpoint pushing is disabled. (An earlier iteration kept imports local-only on a separate `entire/imports/v1` ref; reverted — it caused explain-by-id and `[temporary]`-duplication bugs and was a cross-cutting overhaul. Single-ref is simpler; a local-only/opt-in-to-push mode could be revisited.)
- **Read-only** by design: imported checkpoints have no working-tree snapshot, so they are not rewindable.
- **Claude Code only** this pass (the package and `entire import <agent>` surface leave room for others).

## Reviewer notes

- `Kind:"imported"` + `Provenance` + an `Imported` umbrella flag were added to the checkpoint metadata contract (`api/checkpoint`).
- Verified locally: `mise run lint` (0 issues) and `mise run test:ci` (unit + integration + e2e canary) green; an end-to-end integration test covers dry-run, import, `[imported]` labeling (no `[temporary]` duplication), explain-by-id, idempotency, and rewind refusal.

1	// Package agentimport imports a coding agent's pre-existing local transcripts
2	// into Entire as read-only, commit-less checkpoints on the v1 metadata branch.
3	//
4	// The orchestration (discovery loop, idempotent per-turn IDs, redaction, and
5	// the checkpoint write) is agent-agnostic and lives here. Each agent plugs in
6	// an Importer that knows where its transcripts live and how to split one into
7	// per-user-prompt turns. Claude Code is the only implementation today
8	// (see claude.go); others register themselves the same way.
9	package agentimport
10	
11	import (
12		"context"
13		"crypto/sha256"
14		"encoding/hex"
15		"fmt"
16		"os"
17		"sort"
18		"time"

23		cp "github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint"
24		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/id"
25		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/session"
26		"github.com/entireio/cli/redact"
27	)
28	
29	// LookbackDays bounds how far back import reaches. Fixed this pass (no flag).
30	const LookbackDays = 30
31	
32	// SessionFile is one discovered agent transcript for a repo.
33	type SessionFile struct {
34		Path      string // absolute path to the transcript file
35		SessionID string // agent session id (used in checkpoint metadata)
36	}
37	
38	// Turn is one user-prompt turn extracted from a session transcript. Line
39	// offsets are in raw-line space (newline-counted), matching transcript slicing
40	// and the agent token-usage helpers.
41	type Turn struct {
42		LineStart, LineEnd int
43		UUID               string
44		Prompt, Model      string
45		CreatedAt          time.Time
46		Tokens             *types.TokenUsage
47	}
48	
49	// Importer is the per-agent seam: it locates an agent's transcripts for a repo
50	// and splits one into per-turn units. Everything else (idempotency, redaction,
51	// writing) is handled generically by Run.
52	type Importer interface {
53		// Name is the registry key and the provenance source (e.g. "claude-code").
54		Name() string
55		// AgentType is the display name stored in checkpoint metadata (e.g. "Claude Code").
56		AgentType() types.AgentType
57		// Discover returns the agent's transcript files for the repo within the
58		// lookback window. overridePath replaces the default transcript dir;
59		// sessionFilter, when non-empty, keeps only matching session IDs.
60		Discover(repoRoot, overridePath string, now time.Time, sessionFilter []string) ([]SessionFile, error)
61		// SplitTurns splits one session's raw transcript bytes into per-turn units.
62		SplitTurns(sf SessionFile, full []byte) ([]Turn, error)
63	}
64	
65	// importers is the static set of supported agents. Adding an agent is a new
66	// Importer implementation appended here — no init() / runtime registration.
67	var importers = []Importer{
68		claudeImporter{},
69	}
70	
71	// Get returns the importer registered under name.
72	//
73	//nolint:ireturn // Importer is the intended polymorphic seam returned to callers.
74	func Get(name string) (Importer, bool) {
75		for _, imp := range importers {
76			if imp.Name() == name {
77				return imp, true
78			}
79		}
80		return nil, false
81	}
82	
83	// All returns every supported importer, sorted by name.
84	func All() []Importer {
85		out := append([]Importer(nil), importers...)
86		sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool { return out[i].Name() < out[j].Name() })
87		return out
88	}
89	
90	// Options configures an import run.
91	type Options struct {
92		RepoRoot      string
93		OverridePath  string
94		SessionFilter []string
95		Now           time.Time
96		DryRun        bool
97	}
98	
99	// Result summarizes an import run.
100	type Result struct {
101		SessionsScanned int
102		TurnsImported   int
103		TurnsSkipped    int
104	}
105	
106	// DeriveCheckpointID produces a stable 12-hex checkpoint ID for an imported
107	// turn. Re-importing the same (sessionID, turnUUID) yields the same ID, which
108	// is how import stays idempotent.
109	func DeriveCheckpointID(sessionID, turnUUID string) id.CheckpointID {
110		sum := sha256.Sum256([]byte(sessionID + "/" + turnUUID))
111		return id.MustCheckpointID(hex.EncodeToString(sum[:6])) // 6 bytes = 12 lowercase hex chars
112	}
113	
114	// Run imports the given agent's transcripts (within the lookback window) as
115	// read-only checkpoints on the v1 metadata branch (Kind "imported"). It is
116	// idempotent: turns whose deterministic ID already exists are skipped.
117	func Run(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, imp Importer, opts Options) (Result, error) {
118		var res Result
119		files, err := imp.Discover(opts.RepoRoot, opts.OverridePath, opts.Now, opts.SessionFilter)
120		if err != nil {
121			return res, fmt.Errorf("discover %s sessions: %w", imp.Name(), err)
122		}
123	
124		stores, err := cp.Open(ctx, repo, cp.OpenOptions{})
125		if err != nil {
126			return res, fmt.Errorf("open checkpoint store: %w", err)
127		}
128		existing := make(map[string]bool)
129		if infos, listErr := stores.Persistent.List(ctx); listErr == nil {
130			for _, in := range infos {
131				existing[in.CheckpointID.String()] = true
132			}
133		}
134	
135		for _, sf := range files {
136			res.SessionsScanned++
137			full, readErr := os.ReadFile(sf.Path)
138			if readErr != nil {
139				return res, fmt.Errorf("read %s: %w", sf.Path, readErr)
140			}
141			turns, splitErr := imp.SplitTurns(sf, full)
142			if splitErr != nil {
143				return res, fmt.Errorf("split %s session %s: %w", imp.Name(), sf.SessionID, splitErr)
144			}
145			// Redact the session transcript once and reuse it for every turn's
146			// checkpoint (each turn stores the full session transcript with its own
147			// CheckpointTranscriptStart). Redacting per turn would be O(turns).
148			// Computed lazily so a fully-skipped or dry-run file pays nothing.
149			var red redact.RedactedBytes
150			redacted := false
151			for _, turn := range turns {
152				cid := DeriveCheckpointID(sf.SessionID, turn.UUID)
153				if existing[cid.String()] {
154					res.TurnsSkipped++
155					continue
156				}
157				if opts.DryRun {
158					res.TurnsImported++ // counts what would import
159					continue
160				}
161				if !redacted {
162					r, rerr := redact.JSONLBytes(full)
163					if rerr != nil {
164						return res, fmt.Errorf("redact %s transcript: %w", sf.SessionID, rerr)
165					}
166					red = r
167					redacted = true
168				}
169				if err := writeTurn(ctx, stores, imp, cid, sf, red, turn); err != nil {
170					return res, err
171				}
172				existing[cid.String()] = true
173				res.TurnsImported++
174			}
175		}
176		return res, nil
177	}
178	
179	func writeTurn(ctx context.Context, stores *cp.Stores, imp Importer, cid id.CheckpointID, sf SessionFile, red redact.RedactedBytes, turn Turn) error {
180		if err := stores.Persistent.Write(ctx, cp.Session(cp.WriteOptions{
181			CheckpointID:              cid,
182			SessionID:                 sf.SessionID,
183			CreatedAt:                 turn.CreatedAt,
184			Strategy:                  "import",
185			Kind:                      string(session.KindImported),
186			Agent:                     imp.AgentType(),
187			Model:                     turn.Model,
188			Transcript:                red,
189			Prompts:                   []string{turn.Prompt},
190			CheckpointsCount:          1,
191			CheckpointTranscriptStart: turn.LineStart,
192			TokenUsage:                turn.Tokens,
193		})); err != nil {
194			return fmt.Errorf("write imported checkpoint %s: %w", cid, err)
195		}
196		return nil
197	}

# Brainstorming Ideas Into Designs

Help turn ideas into fully formed designs and specs through natural collaborative dialogue.

Start by understanding the current project context, then ask questions one at a time to refine the idea. Once you understand what you're building, present the design and get user approval.

<HARD-GATE>
Do NOT invoke any implementation skill, write any code, scaffold any project, or take any implementation action until you have presented a design and the user has approved it. This applies to EVERY project regardless of perceived simplicity.
</HARD-GATE>

## Anti-Pattern: "This Is Too Simple To Need A Design"

Every project goes through this process. A todo list, a single-function utility, a config change — all of them. "Simple" projects are where unexamined assumptions cause the most wasted work. The design can be short (a few sentences for truly simple projects), but you MUST present it and get approval.

## Checklist

You MUST create a task for each of these items and complete them in order:

1. **Explore project context** — check files, docs, recent commits
2. **Offer the visual companion just-in-time** — NOT upfront. The first time a question would genuinely be clearer shown than described, offer it then (its own message); on approval its browser tab opens for you. If no visual question ever arises, never offer it. See the Visual Companion section below.
3. **Ask clarifying questions** — one at a time, understand purpose/constraints/success criteria
4. **Propose 2-3 approaches** — with trade-offs and your recommendation
5. **Present design** — in sections scaled to their complexity, get user approval after each section
6. **Write design doc** — save to `docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md` and commit
7. **Spec self-review** — quick inline check for placeholders, contradictions, ambiguity, scope (see below)
8. **User reviews written spec** — ask user to review the spec file before proceeding
9. **Transition to implementation** — invoke writing-plans skill to create implementation plan


**The terminal state is invoking writing-plans.** Do NOT invoke frontend-design, mcp-builder, or any other implementation skill. The ONLY skill you invoke after brainstorming is writing-plans.

## The Process

**Understanding the idea:**

- Check out the current project state first (files, docs, recent commits)
- Before asking detailed questions, assess scope: if the request describes multiple independent subsystems (e.g., "build a platform with chat, file storage, billing, and analytics"), flag this immediately. Don't spend questions refining details of a project that needs to be decomposed first.
- If the project is too large for a single spec, help the user decompose into sub-projects: what are the independent pieces, how do they relate, what order should they be built? Then brainstorm the first sub-project through the normal design flow. Each sub-project gets its own spec → plan → implementation cycle.
- For appropriately-scoped projects, ask questions one at a time to refine the idea
- Prefer multiple choice questions when possible, but open-ended is fine too
- Only one question per message - if a topic needs more exploration, break it into multiple questions
- Focus on understanding: purpose, constraints, success criteria

**Exploring approaches:**

- Propose 2-3 different approaches with trade-offs
- Present options conversationally with your recommendation and reasoning
- Lead with your recommended option and explain why

**Presenting the design:**

- Once you believe you understand what you're building, present the design
- Scale each section to its complexity: a few sentences if straightforward, up to 200-300 words if nuanced
- Ask after each section whether it looks right so far
- Cover: architecture, components, data flow, error handling, testing
- Be ready to go back and clarify if something doesn't make sense

**Design for isolation and clarity:**

- Break the system into smaller units that each have one clear purpose, communicate through well-defined interfaces, and can be understood and tested independently
- For each unit, you should be able to answer: what does it do, how do you use it, and what does it depend on?
- Can someone understand what a unit does without reading its internals? Can you change the internals without breaking consumers? If not, the boundaries need work.
- Smaller, well-bounded units are also easier for you to work with - you reason better about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more reliable when files are focused. When a file grows large, that's often a signal that it's doing too much.

**Working in existing codebases:**

- Explore the current structure before proposing changes. Follow existing patterns.
- Where existing code has problems that affect the work (e.g., a file that's grown too large, unclear boundaries, tangled responsibilities), include targeted improvements as part of the design - the way a good developer improves code they're working in.
- Don't propose unrelated refactoring. Stay focused on what serves the current goal.

## After the Design

**Documentation:**

- Write the validated design (spec) to `docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md`
  - (User preferences for spec location override this default)
- Use elements-of-style:writing-clearly-and-concisely skill if available
- Commit the design document to git

**Spec Self-Review:**
After writing the spec document, look at it with fresh eyes:

1. **Placeholder scan:** Any "TBD", "TODO", incomplete sections, or vague requirements? Fix them.
2. **Internal consistency:** Do any sections contradict each other? Does the architecture match the feature descriptions?
3. **Scope check:** Is this focused enough for a single implementation plan, or does it need decomposition?
4. **Ambiguity check:** Could any requirement be interpreted two different ways? If so, pick one and make it explicit.

Fix any issues inline. No need to re-review — just fix and move on.

**User Review Gate:**
After the spec review loop passes, ask the user to review the written spec before proceeding:

> "Spec written and committed to `<path>`. Please review it and let me know if you want to make any changes before we start writing out the implementation plan."

Wait for the user's response. If they request changes, make them and re-run the spec review loop. Only proceed once the user approves.

**Implementation:**

- Invoke the writing-plans skill to create a detailed implementation plan
- Do NOT invoke any other skill. writing-plans is the next step.

## Key Principles

- **One question at a time** - Don't overwhelm with multiple questions
- **Multiple choice preferred** - Easier to answer than open-ended when possible
- **YAGNI ruthlessly** - Remove unnecessary features from all designs
- **Explore alternatives** - Always propose 2-3 approaches before settling
- **Incremental validation** - Present design, get approval before moving on
- **Be flexible** - Go back and clarify when something doesn't make sense

## Visual Companion

A browser-based companion for showing mockups, diagrams, and visual options during brainstorming. Available as a tool — not a mode. Accepting the companion means it's available for questions that benefit from visual treatment; it does NOT mean every question goes through the browser.

**Offering the companion (just-in-time):** Do NOT offer it upfront. Wait until a question would genuinely be clearer shown than told — a real mockup / layout / diagram question, not merely a UI *topic*. The first time that happens, offer it then, as its own message:
> "This next part might be easier if I show you — I can put together mockups, diagrams, and comparisons in a browser tab as we go. It's still new and can be token-intensive. Want me to? I'll open it for you."

**This offer MUST be its own message.** Only the offer — no clarifying question, summary, or other content. Wait for the user's response. If they accept, start the server with `--open` so their browser opens to the first screen automatically. If they decline, continue text-only and don't offer again unless they raise it.

**Per-question decision:** Even after the user accepts, decide FOR EACH QUESTION whether to use the browser or the terminal. The test: **would the user understand this better by seeing it than reading it?**

- **Use the browser** for content that IS visual — mockups, wireframes, layout comparisons, architecture diagrams, side-by-side visual designs
- **Use the terminal** for content that is text — requirements questions, conceptual choices, tradeoff lists, A/B/C/D text options, scope decisions

A question about a UI topic is not automatically a visual question. "What does personality mean in this context?" is a conceptual question — use the terminal. "Which wizard layout works better?" is a visual question — use the browser.

4	**Issue:** entireio/cli#1336

7	## Problem
8	
9	Entire only captures session data when hooks fire during a live session. A user
10	adopting Entire on an existing repo starts from zero: `entire session list`,
11	`entire checkpoint explain`, `search`, and token aggregates show nothing, even
12	though months of Claude Code transcripts already exist under
13	`~/.claude/projects/<slug>/*.jsonl`.
14	
15	We want to let users bring that pre-existing history into Entire so the
16	read/inspect surface (list, explain, search, tokens, and eventually server-side
17	recap/UI) works on day one — **without** pretending the history has rewindable
18	working-tree state.

20	## Goals
21	
22	- A hidden/labs command:
23	  `entire import claude-code [--path DIR] [--dry-run] [--session ID]...`.
24	  Lookback is a fixed one month (an internal constant, not a flag, this pass).
25	- `entire enable` ends with an interactive prompt that, when transcripts for this
26	  repo are detected, offers to import them with a **default one-month lookback**.
27	- Imported turns become **read-only, commit-less ("orphaned") checkpoints**
28	  available to `checkpoint list`/`explain`, `search`, `tokens`.
29	- Imports are **local-only in this first pass** (never pushed) and **not
30	  rewindable**. Push will become an option later; the design must not preclude
31	  it (see "Push topology (keeping push cheap to add later)").
32	- Idempotent: re-running import does not duplicate.
33	
34	## Non-goals (first pass)
35	
36	- Attaching imported checkpoints to Claude co-authored commits.
37	- Agents other than Claude Code (codex, gemini, cursor, …). The command name
38	  `import claude-code` leaves room to add more later.
39	- Auto-pushing imports / a push prompt / lighting up server-side features. Push
40	  is **deferred**, not designed out — the architecture stays flexible enough to
41	  add it (see "Push topology (keeping push cheap to add later)"), but no push prompt or
42	  `--push` flag ships in this pass.
43	
44	## Background: the orphaned-checkpoint model
45	
46	How live checkpoints normally attach to a commit:
47	
48	- A live session writes to a per-commit **shadow branch**
49	  `entire/<base[:7]>-<worktree[:6]>`.
50	- On `git commit`, the `prepare-commit-msg` hook stamps an
51	  `Entire-Checkpoint: <id>` trailer into the message.
52	- The `post-commit` hook reads the trailer and **condenses** the session onto
53	  the permanent orphan branch `entire/checkpoints/v1` at `<id[:2]>/<id[2:]>/`.
54	
55	Key fact: the persistent metadata on `v1` has **no commit-hash field**
56	(`api/checkpoint/metadata.go`). The commit→checkpoint link is implicit and
57	one-way — it exists only as the trailer string in a commit message. A
58	checkpoint that was never attached to a commit is therefore not a malformed
59	record; it is simply a `v1`-style entry that no commit points back to.

# Import existing transcripts for additional agents

**Status:** Design approved, pending implementation plan
**Date:** 2026-06-26
**Follows:** PR #1527 (`import claude-code`), spec `2026-06-25-import-claude-code-transcripts-design.md`

## Problem

PR #1527 shipped `entire import claude-code`, which reads a repo's pre-existing
Claude Code transcripts and writes them as read-only, commit-less checkpoints on
`entire/checkpoints/v1`. The `agentimport` package was deliberately structured so
that adding an agent is a single new `Importer` appended to the `importers` slice
— no command wiring. Only Claude Code was implemented.

We want to extend import to every other agent Entire supports whose history is
readable from disk: **Cursor, Factory AI Droid, Pi, Codex, Copilot CLI, and
Gemini CLI**.

## Goals

- One additional `Importer` per agent, registered in `agentimport.importers`. The
  `entire import <agent>` subcommand surfaces automatically (`import_cmd.go`
  iterates `agentimport.All()`).
- Reuse each agent's **existing** transcript methods (`CalculateTokenUsage` /
  `CalculateTotalTokenUsage`, `ExtractModel`, `transcript.ExtractUserContent`,
  `GetSessionDir`) — import must not re-encode per-agent transcript knowledge that
  the live/post-enable path already encapsulates behind the `agent.Agent`
  interface.
- Imported checkpoints stay identical in kind to Claude's: commit-less,
  `Kind:"imported"`, `[imported]` label, **not rewindable**, idempotent per the
  existing `DeriveCheckpointID(sessionID, turnUUID)` scheme.

## Non-goals

- **OpenCode.** It has no on-disk transcript Entire can read; its transcripts only
  materialize by shelling out to `opencode export <id>`, and its sessions are not
  cleanly attributable to a repo. Importing it would require a different
  mechanism (CLI enumeration + export) and is out of scope.
- Refactoring `claude.go`, `Run`, the `Importer` interface, or the `Turn` struct.
  All are reused unchanged.
- Any change to enable-time prompting, push behavior, or rewindability. Same as
  PR #1527.

## What import inherently cannot reuse from the live path

Two differences are physics, not style, and match the merged Claude import:

1. **Commit-less / not rewindable.** Live turns capture a working-tree snapshot;
   an imported transcript is only the agent's chat log, so there is no historical
   git state to rewind to.
2. **Turn boundaries.** Live turns learn their start offset from hook events as
   they fire. A finished transcript has no hooks, so per-turn import must locate
   turn starts by scanning for user-prompt records. This scan is the only
   per-agent logic each importer adds — exactly what `claude.go`'s
   `isUserPromptLine` already does.

## Design

### Granularity: per-turn by default, per-session where per-turn is awkward

The `Importer.SplitTurns` contract returns `[]Turn`. `Run` iterates turns and
writes one checkpoint each, deriving a stable ID from
`(sessionID, turn.UUID)`. Both granularities already fit this:

- **Per-turn** — emit one `Turn` per user-prompt record, bounded by the next
  (the `claude.go` pattern).
- **Per-session** — emit a single `Turn{Start: 0, End: <len>, UUID: sessionID}`
  covering the whole transcript. `Run` writes exactly one checkpoint; idempotency
  keys on `(sessionID, sessionID)`.

`Turn.LineStart`/`LineEnd` are offsets in the agent's **native** space (raw lines
for JSONL agents, message index for Gemini). `Run` sets
`CheckpointTranscriptStart = turn.LineStart`, which readers already interpret
per-agent-type (`SliceFromLine` vs `geminicli.SliceFromMessage`). No `Run` change
needed.

### Per-agent plan

| Agent | Discover | Offset space | Granularity | User-prompt marker | Tokens | Model |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cursor | per-repo dir (nested `<id>/<id>.jsonl` or flat `<id>.jsonl`) | line | per-turn | `type`/`role == user` + non-empty `ExtractUserContent` | none → nil | none → "" |
| Factory | per-repo dir `<id>.jsonl` | line | per-turn | inner `role == user` + text | `CalculateTotalTokenUsage(.., subagentsDir)` | adjacent `.settings.json` (best-effort) |
| Pi | per-repo dir `<ts>_<uuid>.jsonl` | line | per-turn | `type==message` + `message.role==user` + text | `CalculateTokenUsage` | `ExtractModel` over the turn slice |
| Codex | **global** `~/.codex/sessions/**/rollout-*.jsonl`, filtered by `session_meta.cwd` ⊆ repoRoot | line | per-turn | `response_item` + `role==user` + `input_text` content | `CalculateTokenUsage` | none → "" |
| Copilot | **flat** `~/.copilot/session-state/*/events.jsonl`, filtered by `session.start` `data.context.cwd`/`gitRoot` ⊆ repoRoot | line | per-turn | `type == "user.message"` | `CalculateTokenUsage` | `ExtractModelFromTranscript` (best-effort) |
| Gemini | per-repo hash dir `session-*.json` | message index | **per-session** | n/a (whole session) | `CalculateTokenUsage(data, 0)` | none → "" |

`session ID` derivation per agent: Cursor/Factory = file stem; Pi = `<uuid>` suffix
of stem; Codex = `session_meta.id` (or stem); Copilot = parent dir name; Gemini =
file stem.

### Repo filtering (Codex, Copilot only)

`GetSessionDir` ignores the repo for these two, so Discover reads one metadata
record per candidate session and keeps only those whose working directory is the
repo root or a descendant of it (`repoMatches(cwd, repoRoot)`: `cwd == repoRoot`
or `cwd` under `repoRoot`). Sessions whose directory cannot be determined are
skipped (conservative: never import history we cannot attribute to this repo).
The same `LookbackDays` modtime cutoff and `--session` filter as Claude apply.

### Duplication

Each importer is self-contained, parsing a distinct struct shape; no shared
engine is introduced. If the per-turn turn-assembly loop trips the `dupl` linter
(threshold 75), it gets a justified `//nolint:dupl` comment rather than a shared
extraction — per the "no refactor" constraint.

## Files

New, one per agent, in `cmd/entire/cli/agentimport/`:
`cursor.go`, `factory.go`, `pi.go`, `codex.go`, `copilot.go`, `gemini.go`, each
with a sibling `*_test.go`. Registration: append the six to the `importers` slice
in `agentimport.go`.

## Testing

Mirror `claude_test.go` per agent:

- `Discover`: lookback cutoff, `--session` filter, missing-dir-is-empty, and
  (Codex/Copilot) repo-match include/exclude by cwd.
- `SplitTurns`: turn boundaries bounded by next prompt; tool-result/non-user
  lines do not start a turn; prompt/model/token extraction; Gemini single-turn
  per session.
- Extend the registry test to assert all importers register and produce distinct
  names.

`mise run check` per agent during TDD; `mise run lint` before push.

explain how the import command supports the additional agents (the command / required params etc)

The import command surface is entirely **derived from the importer registry** — there's no per-agent command wiring. Here's how it works.

## Command shape

```
entire import <agent> [--path DIR] [--dry-run] [--session ID]...
```

`newImportCmd()` (in `cmd/entire/cli/import_cmd.go`) builds the parent `import` command, then loops over `agentimport.All()` and adds one subcommand per registered importer:

```go
for _, imp := range agentimport.All() {
    cmd.AddCommand(newImportAgentCmd(imp))
}
```

Because I appended the six new importers to the `importers` slice in `agentimport.go`, all seven subcommands appear automatically — no command code changed:

```
entire import claude-code | codex | copilot-cli | cursor | factoryai-droid | gemini | pi
```

The subcommand name is `imp.Name()` (the agent registry key, e.g. `"copilot-cli"`), and the help text interpolates `imp.AgentType()` (e.g. `"Copilot CLI"`).

## Parameters

**Positional args:** none. `Args: cobra.NoArgs`. The agent is the subcommand itself.

**The repo is implicit** — not a param. The command resolves it from the current working directory via `paths.WorktreeRoot(ctx)`, and errors out if you're not in a git repo. That `repoRoot` is what scopes the import:
- For per-repo-dir agents (Cursor, Factory, Pi, Gemini) it's passed to the agent's `GetSessionDir(repoRoot)` to locate that repo's transcript directory.
- For global/flat-store agents (Codex, Copilot) it's used to **filter** sessions by their recorded cwd/gitRoot (`repoMatches`), since those agents store all repos' sessions together.

**Flags** (all optional, identical across every agent):

| Flag | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `--path DIR` | agent's default dir | Override the transcript directory to import from (maps to `Options.OverridePath`). Useful when transcripts live somewhere non-standard, or for testing. |
| `--dry-run` | false | Report what *would* import without writing checkpoints. |
| `--session ID` (repeatable) | all | Import only the named session IDs. The ID matched is whatever each importer derives as its `SessionID` (see below). |

**Lookback** is *not* a flag — it's a fixed `LookbackDays = 30` constant (inherited from the original Claude import). Sessions whose transcript file modtime is older than 30 days are skipped.

## What each subcommand does at runtime

The `RunE` is shared — it just dispatches to the generic orchestrator:

```go
strategy.EnsureRedactionConfigured()           // load repo/user redaction config first
res, err := agentimport.Run(ctx, repo, imp, agentimport.Options{
    RepoRoot: repoRoot, OverridePath: pathFlag, SessionFilter: sessions,
    Now: time.Now(), DryRun: dryRun,
})
```

`Run` calls `imp.Discover(...)` → reads each session file → `imp.SplitTurns(...)` → redacts → writes one read-only, commit-less checkpoint per turn (idempotent on `sha256(sessionID + "/" + turnUUID)`). Output:

```
Imported 12 turn(s) from 3 session(s) (5 already imported).
```

So all agent-specific knowledge lives behind the `Importer` interface (`Name`, `AgentType`, `Discover`, `SplitTurns`); the command, flags, redaction, idempotency, and checkpoint write are agent-agnostic and unchanged.

## The one cross-agent subtlety: what `--session ID` matches

The `SessionID` an importer derives differs by agent, which determines what you pass to `--session`:

- **Cursor / Factory / Gemini** — the file stem (`<id>.jsonl` → `id`; Gemini `session-<date>-<shortid>.json` → the full stem)
- **Pi** — the `<uuid>` suffix of the `<timestamp>_<uuid>.jsonl` filename
- **Codex** — the `id` from the session's `session_meta` line
- **Copilot** — the session-state subdirectory name (`<id>/events.jsonl` → `id`)

That's the only place the agents diverge at the CLI level; everything else is uniform.
